results.title: Repeatability, Reproducibility, and Replicability: Tackling the 3R challenge in biointerface science and engineering | Biointerphases | AIP Publishing
results.content: # Repeatability, Reproducibility, and Replicability: Tackling the 3R challenge in biointerface science and engineering *Open Access*. McArthur; Repeatability, Reproducibility, and Replicability: Tackling the 3R challenge in biointerface science and engineering. Over the past few years, there have been many papers1,2 and editorials3 that have shown that issues associated with Repeatability, Reproducibility, and Replicability impact almost all areas of science, and in an AVS-conducted survey, 65% of those responding indicated that they have seen or experienced significant reproducibility issues when they have sought to recreate experiments from the literature. The challenge in the Biointerface Science community is compounded by the inherent variability of biology. A recent article in Nature Nanotechnology highlighted the need for minimal information reporting standards in publication as a means of ensuring authors provide key components of their experimental protocols.2 In partnership with our sister journals JVST A and B and Surface Science Spectra (SSS), we will create standardized reporting systems for techniques and data collection with all of our publications and encourage you to submit your XPS and TOF-SIMS data to SSS for others to use as reference materials. At the upcoming AVS International Symposium in October 2019, there will be an In Focus topic entitled New Challenges to Reproducible Data and Analysis and I encourage you all to participate in this session, either by submitting an abstract or by attending the sessions and joining in the discussions. As a journal, we will champion best practices, sharing our knowledge across our community, and seek to support researchers who are new to the field or want to explore new techniques to avoid the pitfalls and better understand both the opportunities and limitations of the techniques, methods, and approaches used in our multidisciplinary community. This year we will be focusing on developing our themed collections, continuing to build and highlight themes including SIMS, Microbial Interactions, and Women in Biointerface Science. We will launch a new collection to shine a spotlight on Early Career Researchers across the globe, exploring the challenges for quantitative characterization in 3D cell culture and creating a new approach to categorizing our articles and sharing the history of publications in select fields via new themed collections. In 2018, we published nine papers as Scilights (), in which science journalists worked with authors to develop media-ready articles from our published papers.
